summary: Isomer's CoreGraphics is the part of Apple's CoreGraphics that Swift code, SwiftUI's interface above all, reaches for: `CGFloat` and the geometry types with their C-style functions, `CGAffineTransform`, `CGColor` and `CGColorSpace`, `CGPath` and `CGMutablePath`, line caps and joins, blend modes. It is written in Swift; CoreGraphics' C API that rests on CoreFoundation or callbacks into C is left out. On Apple platforms an app uses Apple's CoreGraphics.
deviations: `CGFloat` is a `Double` on every architecture, as Apple's is on every platform Apple ships (swift-corelibs-foundation makes it a `Float` on 32-bit architectures, wasm32 among them): a layout computed in WebAssembly is the one computed natively. On 32-bit architectures its bit-level API (`bitPattern`, `RawSignificand`, `significandBitPattern`) is therefore 64 bits wide (`UInt64`) rather than `UInt`.
`CGColor` keeps the components it was made with: there is no color management, and a device RGB color is drawn as sRGB.

`CGPath` stores what CoreGraphics stores (moves, lines, quadratic and cubic curves, closes); arcs, ellipses and rounded rectangles become cubic curves as CoreGraphics makes them. `contains(_:using:transform:)` flattens curves into 16 or 24 segments.
`CGPathElement.points` comes from `applyWithBlock` only: the C-function form, `apply(info:function:)`, would need a C function pointer over a Swift type.

groups.title: CoreFoundation types
groups.why: These take or return CoreFoundation values (`CFString` color space names, `CFDictionary` representations and options, `CFData` ICC profiles, `CFTypeID`). Isomer has no CoreFoundation: its Foundation is Swift, and CoreGraphics here takes Swift types.

groups.title: PDF
groups.why: PDF documents, pages, content streams, scanners and PDF contexts are a document format of their own, read and written through CoreFoundation-typed C API. An Isomer app shows a PDF through the platform (a web view, the system's viewer).

groups.title: Fonts, glyphs and text drawing
groups.why: Glyphs and fonts are CoreText's; Isomer lays text out in each platform's renderer.

groups.title: Data providers and consumers, C callbacks
groups.why: Streams of bytes in and out of CoreGraphics through C callback tables and CoreFoundation data and URLs. Isomer's images (when they come) take `Data`.

groups.title: HDR, tone mapping and color conversion
groups.why: High dynamic range content, tone mapping and conversions between color spaces need color management Isomer does not have.

groups.title: Surfaces, layers, patterns and shadings
groups.why: IOSurface is Apple's; layers, patterns and shadings draw through C callbacks into a CoreGraphics context.

groups.title: Errors
groups.why: CoreGraphics' C error codes go with the C API Isomer leaves out.

groups.title: Images and bitmap descriptions
groups.why: `CGImage` as a pixel buffer, which SwiftUI's `Image(decorative:scale:)` and `GraphicsContext` take; with it the bitmap descriptions (`CGBitmapInfo`, `CGImageAlphaInfo`, `CGImageByteOrderInfo`…).

groups.title: Gradients
groups.why: `CGGradient`, with images, for SwiftUI's gradients over CoreGraphics types.

groups.title: Drawing into a context
groups.why: `CGContext` as a bitmap renderer written in Swift: a substantial piece of work, needed by apps that draw with CoreGraphics directly.

groups.title: Path operations
groups.why: Stroking, dashing, flattening and the boolean operations on paths, and `CGPath`'s C-function enumerator.

groups.title: Codable colors and color spaces
groups.why: Apple's `CGColor` and `CGColorSpace` are `Codable`; Isomer's are not yet.

groups.title: Color space details
groups.why: Color spaces made from ICC data, calibrated, indexed or pattern spaces, and what they report about themselves.

additions: Declarations Isomer's CoreGraphics has that Apple's does not; each is a part of Isomer's implementation (or a helper SwiftUI needs) and is meant to move behind `@_spi(Isomer)`.
